stem.en: A student says, "Plant cells have chloroplasts to make food, so they do not need mitochondria." Why is this statement false?

text.en: Chloroplasts make food, but mitochondria release its energy.

feedback.en: Yes. Making food and releasing its energy are two separate jobs.

text.en: Plants have no chloroplasts at all and use only mitochondria.

feedback.en: Green plant cells do have chloroplasts. They make the food.

text.en: Plants use mitochondria only in winter, when the sun is weak.

feedback.en: Plant cells use mitochondria all the time, in every season.

text.en: Only roots have mitochondria, and leaves have only chloroplasts.

feedback.en: Leaf cells have both. Their mitochondria work beside their chloroplasts.

explanation.en: A chloroplast makes food using sunlight. A cell still has to release the energy in that food, and mitochondria do this. So plant cells need both organelles.

hints.en: What does a chloroplast make, and what must happen to it before a cell can use its energy?
